title.narrative: Strengthening Community Resilience and Survivor-Centered GBV Response for Conflict-Affected Women, Girls, and Vulnerable Groups in Madagali and Gwoza LGAs of Borno and Adamawa States, Nigeria

description.narrative: ltpgtAGAJI GLOBAL UNITY FOUNDATION (AGUF), in partnership with Aid for African Women Girls (A2WG), proposes a 6-month lifesaving GBV intervention designed to deliver survivor-centered services while institutionalizing inclusive, community-led protection systems in Madagali LGA of Adamawa State and Gwoza LGA of Borno State.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe overall goal of the project is to enhance the protection, resilience, and well-being of women, girls, and other vulnerable groups by strengthening community-based GBV prevention and response mechanisms during the lean season. The main objective is to expand access to lifesaving, survivor-centered GBV services while reinforcing sustainable community structures that mitigate risks and support safe, inclusive referral pathways.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project is organized around four mutually reinforcing outcomes:ltbrgtltbgtOutcome 1lt/bgt ensures survivors and at-risk groups access lifesaving and well-coordinated GBV response services through the establishment/revival and operation of two Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS) that provide case management, psychosocial support, dignity kits, and medical referrals.ltbrgtltbgtOutcome 2lt/bgt enhances survivor well-being and resilience by delivering structured psychosocial care, vocational and life skills sessions, and livelihoods support, reducing reliance on harmful coping strategies.ltbrgtltbgtOutcome 3lt/bgt strengthens community resilience and accountability through the establishment and institutionalization of Community Protection Resilience Networks (CPRNs), inclusive platforms comprising community leaders, women’s groups, youth, disability representatives, and local vigilantes serving as sustainable gatekeepers of GBV prevention, response, and risk mitigation.ltbrgtltbgtOutcome 4lt/bgt integrates GBV risk mitigation into multi-sectoral humanitarian response, ensuring women, girls, and marginalized groups are protected during food, nutrition, WASH, and other lifesaving service delivery in the lean season.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtAGUF and A2WG will implement complementary roles to ensure efficiency and coverage. AGUF will lead in Madagali, focusing on WGSS establishment and delivery of direct survivor-centered services. A2WG will take the lead in Gwoza, spearheading CPRN institutionalization, community mobilization, and sectoral advocacy. This division avoids duplication, maximizes organizational strengths, and ensures equal emphasis on service delivery and community system strengthening.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project is designed for immediate lifesaving impact, while embedding sustainability beyond the six-month implementation period. By anchoring services in safe spaces, building community-owned CPRNs, and reinforcing referral and coordination systems, the intervention ensures that survivors and at-risk individuals will continue to access protection and resilience mechanisms long after project closure.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThrough this approach, the project directly advances the GBV Sub-Sector Objectives SSO9 (improved access to lifesaving services), SSO10 (enhancing survivor well-being), and SSO11 (strengthening community resilience and systems), while contributing to the NHF Lean Season Allocation’s overarching goal of reducing excess morbidity and mortality among the most vulnerable populations.ltbrgtlt/pgt
